name: Worker Info Exchange
tagline: Using data rights law to give gig economy workers transparency and control over the algorithmic systems that manage their work.
dependency_risks: Reliance on GDPR and UK data protection law
Litigation-dependent model requires ongoing legal support
policy_outcomes: Amsterdam District Court (2023) ordered Uber and Ola Cabs to disclose algorithmic management data to drivers
Court of Appeal Amsterdam ruled platforms cannot use trade secrets exemptions to deny drivers data access
First court order overturning an automated worker dismissal decision under GDPR Article 22
Uber ordered to disclose basis for unfair dismissals, wage deductions, and surveillance systems
outcome_methodology: strategic litigation using GDPR Data Subject Access Requests; large-scale data audit (1.5M+ trips, 258 drivers, 2016-2024)
documented_limitations: Litigation process is slow and costly
Wins require ongoing enforcement to be effective
failure_modes: Platform companies appeal and delay compliance
Regulatory capture or weakening of GDPR
governance_model: UK-registered limited company; founder-led; operates as nonprofit / NGO
